key_insight: Floating solar PV could be a highly scalable clean-power option for South America, combining strong energy yield with land, water, and grid benefits.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a decision framework for sizing and siting floating PV near hydropower and other infrastructure to improve energy access and system flexibility.
method: Assessed FSPV potential and deployment value across South America.
Modeled case studies in Nicaragua, Honduras, and Guyana.
Compared techno-economic and system benefits including emissions, land savings, and water-security impacts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports estimated annual yields above 1,500 to 2,000 kWh per kW with capacity factors above 20% for 50 to 398 MW systems, plus strong regional potential of about 38.26 TWh per million acres of water surface.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may face site-specific constraints such as water-body suitability, grid interconnection, environmental permitting, and operations under local climate and infrastructure conditions.
paper_title: Pushing the Frontiers for Floating Solar Photovoltaics -- The Case for South America
